chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ṣafwān, from Manṣūr, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:

If a man becomes certain that he has omitted a rakʿah from the salat (prayer), and he has already performed two sajdahs and omitted the rukuʿ, then he restarts the salat (prayer). This does not contradict what we have said, because we interpret this report as referring to one who forgot the rukuʿ in a salat (prayer) in which inadvertence is not allowed, such as the dawn prayer or the maghrib prayer, or concerning the first two rakʿahs, according to what we stated in the earlier reports. And that which clarifies what we have mentioned...

key_terms.اسْتَأْنَفَ: he recommenced or restarted from the beginning
key_terms.السَّهْوُ: inadvertence or forgetfulness in ritual performance
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيْنِ: the two prostrations performed in a rakʿah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone remembers after two sajdahs that he omitted the rukuʿ in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling for one who becomes certain that he omitted the rukuʿ after having already performed the two sajdahs in salat (prayer). It indicates that the salat should be restarted, and explains that this is understood in the case of prayers or rakʿahs in which such omission cannot be remedied through sahw considerations.
